packages.title: Add priority field to Task model
packages.description: In the Task dataclass in src/todo/models.py, add a field `priority: str = "normal"` as the LAST field (after `tags`), so existing positional/keyword constructions like Task(1, "a", done=True, tags=["x"]) keep working. Allowed values are exactly "low", "normal", "high". Add a `__post_init__` that raises ValueError if priority is not one of those three (so both Task(...) and Task.from_dict(...) with a bad priority raise ValueError). to_dict must include the key "priority" (dict becomes {"id", "title", "done", "tags", "priority"}). from_dict must read priority with d.get("priority", "normal"), so a dict with no "priority" key (files saved before this change) loads with priority "normal".

must_cover: Task created without priority has priority 'normal'
Task can be created with priority 'low', 'normal', and 'high'
Task(1, 'a', priority='urgent') raises ValueError
Task.to_dict includes 'priority'
Task.from_dict of a dict without a 'priority' key gives priority 'normal'
Task.from_dict with an invalid priority raises ValueError
Roundtrip to_dict/from_dict preserves priority 'high'

packages.title: Update TodoService to handle task priorities
packages.description: Change TodoService.add in src/todo/service.py to the signature add(self, title, tags=(), priority="normal") and pass priority=priority when constructing the new Task (Task already has a `priority` field that validates and raises ValueError for values other than "low"/"normal"/"high"). The task is saved via the existing storage.save call; Task.to_dict already includes priority, so no storage changes are needed. Keep all other behavior (title stripping, empty-title ValueError) unchanged.

must_cover: svc.add('a') returns a task with priority 'normal'
svc.add('a', priority='high') returns a task with priority 'high'
After add with priority='high', svc.list() (reloaded from storage) shows priority 'high'

packages.title: Add sort_tasks to query module
packages.description: Add a function sort_tasks(tasks, by="id") to src/todo/query.py (keep filter_tasks unchanged). It returns a NEW sorted list (use sorted(); never modify the input list). by="priority": high first, then normal, then low, ties broken by id ascending (e.g. key = (rank[t.priority], t.id) with rank = {"high": 0, "normal": 1, "low": 2}). by="title": sort by t.title. by="id": sort by t.id. Any other value of `by` raises ValueError. Tasks have attributes id (int), title (str), priority (one of "low", "normal", "high").

must_cover: by='priority' orders high, normal, low with ties broken by id ascending
by='title' sorts by title
by='id' (and the default) sorts by id
the input list is not modified and a new list is returned
an invalid `by` value raises ValueError

packages.title: Mark high-priority tasks in format_task
packages.description: In format_task in src/todo/formatting.py, when task.priority == "high", put "!" immediately before the title, e.g. Task(1, "Buy milk", priority="high") formats as "  1 [ ] !Buy milk" (tags still follow as before, e.g. "  1 [ ] !a #x"). Tasks with priority "normal" or "low" format exactly as before. Do not change format_list.

must_cover: format_task(Task(1, 'Buy milk', priority='high')) == '  1 [ ] !Buy milk'
a high-priority task with tags keeps the tags after the title
normal and low priority tasks format without '!' (e.g. '  1 [ ] a #x')

packages.title: Add priority column to CSV export
packages.description: In to_csv in src/todo/export.py, add a priority column right after title. The header row becomes exactly "id,title,priority,done,tags" and each row writes [t.id, t.title, t.priority, t.done, ";".join(t.tags)]. Example: to_csv([Task(1, "a", tags=["x", "y"])]) == "id,title,priority,done,tags\n1,a,normal,False,x;y\n". Do not change to_markdown.

must_cover: header is 'id,title,priority,done,tags'
a default task row contains 'normal' in the priority column right after title
a high-priority task row contains 'high' in the priority column

packages.title: Add counts_by_priority to stats
packages.description: Add counts_by_priority(tasks) to src/todo/stats.py. It returns a dict with all three keys "high", "normal", "low" always present, each mapped to the number of tasks with that t.priority (0 if none), e.g. {"high": 1, "normal": 2, "low": 0}. An empty list gives {"high": 0, "normal": 0, "low": 0}. Leave existing functions unchanged.

must_cover: counts tasks correctly per priority, e.g. one high and two normal gives {'high': 1, 'normal': 2, 'low': 0}
unused priorities are present with 0
empty list gives all three keys with 0

packages.title: Add --priority and --sort to the CLI
packages.description: In src/todo/cli.py build_parser: the `add` subparser gets `--priority` with choices=["low", "normal", "high"], default "normal"; the `list` subparser gets `--sort` with choices=["id", "priority", "title"], default "id". In main: for add call svc.add(args.title, tags=args.tag, priority=args.priority); for list return format_list(sort_tasks(svc.list(tag=args.tag, include_done=not args.pending), by=args.sort)), importing sort_tasks from todo.query (signature sort_tasks(tasks, by="id"), returns a new sorted list; "priority" orders high, normal, low, ties by id). Note format_task prefixes the title of high-priority tasks with "!" (e.g. "  1 [ ] !milk"). Keep everything else unchanged.

must_cover: add with --priority high then list shows '  1 [ ] !milk'
add without --priority gives a normal task (no '!')
list --sort priority orders high before normal before low
list --sort title orders by title; list without --sort orders by id
an invalid --priority value makes argparse exit (SystemExit)

notes: p1: specified priority must be the last dataclass field with default 'normal' (keeps positional Task(...) calls working), validation in __post_init__ so from_dict also raises, and from_dict uses d.get('priority', 'normal'); added must_cover for constructor ValueError and the missing-key default; removed test_roundtrip from existing_tests_to_update (it won't break).
p2: spelled out passing priority=priority to Task and that storage needs no change; removed test_add_complete from existing_tests_to_update (it won't break).
p3: added sort key guidance and a must_cover for not mutating the input.
p4: clarified '!' placement with tags and that format_list is unchanged; removed test_format from existing_tests_to_update (it won't break).
p5: gave exact row layout and expected CSV string; test_export is correctly listed as breaking.
p6: stated empty-list result and that all three keys are always present.

p7: gave exact argparse choices/defaults, how main wires priority into svc.add and sort_tasks into list, and the sort_tasks signature; expanded must_cover; removed test_add_list from existing_tests_to_update (it won't break).
